Welcome to the Newcastle United v Arsenal preview.

Saturday 21st November and a 5.30pm kick-off.

Newcastle United host Arsenal on Saturday  looking to get a stop-start season back on track against the table-topping champions.

The Toon have picked up a disappointing five points from five home league matches so far this season having lost the last two without scoring a goal.

Saturday represents a huge chance to put that right against an Arsenal side who haven’t got the best of recent records on Tyneside.

It has been revealed that A late kick-off allows some extra time in various Tyneside hostelries which usually contributes to a cracking atmosphere. Lets hope Toon fans will be loud, proud and celebrating come full-time .

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their past six league matches. Wins have come over Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Fulham. Frustratingly, we’ve also suffered deserved defeats against Coventry, Villa and Everton. We’ve scored six goals in these games and conceded eight. The seven points gained has us languishing in a disappointing twelfth league position but a win could fire us up the table.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal are the form team in the league right now having won five in a row. Since losing to Brighton in September, they’ve gone on to beat Leeds, Everton, Forest, Liverpool and Hull. They’ve conceded four goals in these matches and scored seven, they’ve kept four clean sheets in the row. They are right now five points clear at the top of the table and will be hoping to have extended that lead come Saturday night.

In a recent development, newcastle travelled to Fulham before the international break hoping to achieve their fourth straight success in the capital after wins over Spurs, Millwall and Crystal Palace. United started brightly with Harvey Barnes forcing two good saves before Dan Burn thought he’d given us the lead only for his effort to be ruled out for a foul in the build-up from Wissa. At the other end, Hornicek was in fine form making a string of good saves as the sides went into the half-time break goalless. The second half continued in a similar vein with both sides sensing they could win and when the breakthrough was finally made, it was the Toon fans celebrating. Jacob Murphy picked up the ball and beat two men before unleashing an incredible strike into the top corner with just ten minutes to play. Unfortunately the party in the away end was to be very short-lived indeed as just a few minutes later, Fulham equalised to set up a grandstand finish where both teams had chances to grab a late winner. Lewis Hall was played in on goal on the stroke of ninety minutes only to see his weak effort easily stopped before Hornicek pulled off an incredible save to salvage a point for the Toon who had to be content with a 1-1 draw.

Arsenal hosted Hull City in their last match and were frustrated by the Tigers for much of the ninety minutes. They scored late on to seal a 1-0 victory and had cause for further celebration when Man City lost a few hours later. The champions are determined to maintain their grip on the trophy.

-Newcastle have won four of their last six home games against the Gunners in all competitions.

-NUFC have found the net in their last four home matches against Arsenal.

-The Toon have beaten Arsenal at home on nine Premier League occasions.

It has been revealed that graeme Souness was enduring a rotten start to the 05/06 season when Arsenal visited St James’ Park in December. The Toon had failed to score in their opening five matches of the campaign but the arrival of Michael Owen seemed to have brought about a change in fortunes with five wins and two draws in our next ten games. Despite this, Souness was on borrowed time and this match against the Gunners would end up being one of the highlights of his ill-fated reign as manager. Newcastle spent most of the first half on the back foot and were grateful to Shay Given for a number of saves (one in particular even being applauded from Arsenal striker Thierry Henry!) but the Toon were getting stuck in and this physical approach was rattling the Reds who weren’t used to not having their own way.

In a recent development, at the start of the second half, the match descended into a real blood and thunder encounter which proved too much for Arsenal midfielder Gilberto Silva who was sent off for two bookable offences. Arsenal were then furious that an Alan Shearer foul on Sol Campbell wasn’t punished with a card and decided to fight fire with fire leading to a disgraceful assault on Scott Parker from the Arsenal ‘keeper that left our man short of a couple of teeth! Incredibly Parker played on with a mouth full of cotton wool as he bravely battled for every ball until another Arsenal foul left him sprawled out on the turf signalling to be subbed off. By now, Newcastle really had the bit between their teeth (if Scott Parker can pardon the expression!) and the crowd could sense a goal was coming.

Industry observers note that with just nine minutes left, Shearer’s physicality allowed him to hold the ball up on the edge of the area and lay it off to Solano who fired home a spectacular effort at the Leazes End to spark wild and ecstatic celebrations. Not for the first (or last) time, Arsenal proved they don’t like it up ‘em at St James’ and Febregas threw a strop when unwisely attempting to start a fight with Alan Shearer before the match had even restarted. As the away side huffed and puffed looking for an equaliser, it became apparent that this would be Newcastle’s day and Micheal Owen even had a chance to double the lead near the end that unfortunately he couldn’t take. The final whistle brought an outpouring of joy and relief as the Toon Army celebrated a Merry Christmas victory. A week later, we’d go to West Ham and a Micheal Owen hat-trick was the cornerstone of a brilliant 4-2 win. If Graeme Souness felt his luck was turning however then he had another thing coming. Owen would break his foot a week later and Souness was given the sack having achieved just one point from the next six matches. Glenn Roeder would come in and steady the ship with a tremendous end to a tumultuous season but that’s a story for another day. Newcastle 1-0 Arsenal.

Malcolm Macdonald – Some of our older readers will have fond memories of this legendary number nine. ‘Supermac’, as he was affectionately known by fans, kick-started his Toon career with a hat-trick in his first home match against Liverpool. What was to follow has gone down in Toon Army folklore! Scoring one hundred and twenty-one goals in just two hundred and twenty-seven appearances has him up there with the best of the best in NUFC history. Perhaps his finest hour came in the 1974 FA Cup Semi-Final when he scored two second half goals to defeat Burnley 2-0 at Hillsborough and send United to their first FA Cup final for nineteen years. Unfortunately, he couldn’t repeat this feat at Wembley as a tame performance was punished by a 3-0 defeat to a Kevin Keegan inspired Liverpool. There was uproar when he was sold to Arsenal for a third of a million pounds in 1976. He went on to score forty-two goals in eighty-four league games for the Gunners.

Andy Cole began his career by playing one league game for Arsenal before being loaned to Fulham and then sold to Bristol City. Kevin Keegan broke the club’s transfer record by splashing out £1.75 million for the striker in 1993. This is a number nine who’s record stands up to anyone else’s – a whopping sixty-eight goals in eighty-four matches before being controversially sold to Man United in January 1995 for a British record transfer fee. Some fans were so angry at the sale that they turned up at the stadium demanding answers which Keegan provided, famously standing on the steps to explain his decision. King Kev would go on to sign both Sir Les and Alan Shearer as the entertainers came ‘so close’ to being champions of England for the first time since 1927 and the debate still rages on about which of the three was the best number nine of NUFC’s Premier League era.

Sol Campbell was something of a legend at Arsenal having run down his contract at arch-rivals Tottenham to join the Gunners on a free transfer. He’d go on to win a number of trophies and even grabbed a goal in the 2006 Champions League final. He played a handful of games for NUFC in 2010 but it’s safe to say he was well past his best when donning the famous black and white.

Matthias Jaissle after a 1-1 draw away at Fulham: “A step in the right direction after the last performance. That’s something we can really build on.I think there were occasions also to win that game. Of course, the disallowed goal, a soft one, I would say. I see it differently then also a big chance at the end. Then you should go home with three points but one point and a performance is something we can work on. It’s now time to reflect and recharge also with a long season ahead of us, then pull out the things we need to improve and there are a couple of aspects, but today highlighted a clear direction in the right way so we can build on that. We did enough to win. We spoke clearly through the week and we saw that today, there was complete commitment and togetherness in all phases. The first 20 minutes there was a lack of confidence from last week but we grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on.”.

Mikel Arteta after a 1-0 win at home to Hull City:  “Not beautiful but effective. I’m delighted with the win because to go to the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or for a player. I think, regarding the performance, we were the better team. I think we had enough chances and situations to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren’t efficient enough to do that, and then we have to rely on generating volume, generating a lot of situations in and around the box until we are able to break them down.This is exactly how we won the game, and Martin, the way he scores, is not the most beautiful one but the most effective one, which is a simple shot and then following the next action, and that was enough today to win again.”.

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank.

There can be no doubt that Newcastle have been poor recently despite showing some promising signs of improvement against Fulham last match. Games after an international break are notoriously difficult to predict. The bookies may be looking at this as something of a formality but we seem to do a lot better against the bigger sides and have a great recent record at home against the Gunners. I was thinking this may be a score draw but my confidence has been growing throughout the week so I’m going for a wildly-celebrated win followed by a few sore heads on Sunday morning. Newcastle 2-1 Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola will know the importance of winning at Anfield considering he has already lost against Manchester City and Arsenal, and he cannot afford a loss against the Red Devils at their lowest moment.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Man United.

© Imago / David Rawcliffe, Propaganda Photo.

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, though despite missing his side's win against Crystal Palace before the November international break, he could make his return against Man United.

© Iconsport / Marty Jean-Louis/Sipa USA.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United).

Recent findings suggest that possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City).

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some weeks, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

It has been revealed that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The initiative was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one].".

The defender has since returned to parts of team training, though he is far behind the rest of the squad.

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Much like Leoni, the right-back has returned to parts of team training, but Liverpool are set to take a cautious approach to his fitness.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 05:52 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 05:53 EST, 18 November 2026.

Former Manchester United and Chelsea star Juan Mata has retired from football at the age of 38.

The Spain star, who came through Real Madrid's academy before winning the Champions League with Chelsea and the Europa League with both the Blues and Man United, enjoyed a dazzling career in England before moving to clubs in Turkey, Japan and Australia.

The midfielder also distinguished himself for his national side, winning the 2010 World Cup as part of the squad, and scoring in Spain's victorious Euro 2012 final against Italy.

Most recently featuring in Australia's A-League for Melbourne Victory, Mata announced the end of his playing career with a poignant video filmed inside a dressing room to the sound of Elvis Presley's 'Now or Never'.

In the clip, Mata symbolically hangs his boots on a hook in the locker room before leaving, with the video captioned: 'Sometimes, to love is to let go.

Sometimes, to love… is to let go. THANKS FOOTBALL. ⚽️❤️♾️A veces, amar… es dejar ir. GRACIAS FÚTBOL. ⚽️❤️♾️ pic.twitter.com/v7otd6AyOq.

Juan Mata has unveiled his retirement from football with a poignant video message (Source: Juan Mata).

The former Chelsea and Man United midfielder enjoyed a decorated career on English soil.

A popular presence wherever he plied his trade, Mata's comments on social media were soon flooded with well-wishes from former clubs.

In a recent development, 'Great player, better person,' Man United shared under his post on X. 'Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan (red heart emoji).'.

According to recent reports, chelsea had a similar send-off for him, with the club writing: 'So many special memories. Thank you, Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Industry observers note that former Chelsea executive Marina Granovskaia added her personal thanks with a message too, writing: 'Great video! Great career too! (red heart emoji). Wishing you all the best Juan (blue heart emoji).'.

Former team-mates including Ander Herrera, Ashley Young, Santi Cazorla and Mario Suarez were among those to send messages of thanks and congratulations, with Man City star Vivianne Miedema also writing to Mata.

'Congratulations on an amazing career and changing football on and off the pitch (hand clap emoji, green heart emoji),' the Dutch WSL trailblazer wrote.

Despite starting his youth career at Real Madrid, Mata's first senior minutes in the Spanish top flight came with his move in 2007 to Valencia.

Mata notched up 174 appearances for the side and won the Copa del Rey in club colours before his landmark move to Chelsea.

In west London, the midfielder won the FA Cup and Champions League in his first season, and the Europa League in his second.

The video contained a brief farewell message and was widely liked by his former team-mates.

After leaving Chelsea, the Spaniard enjoyed a strong stint at Manchester United.

At the end of last month, the Euro 2012 winner was treated to a lap of appreciation at his last club Melbourne Victory.

But a falling-out with then-coach Jose Mourinho called time on his stint at Stamford Bridge and a move north to join Man United – where he would later reunite with the Portuguese manager during his stint in Manchester between 2016 and 2018.

Mata later enjoyed stints at Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before his move to Melbourne.

In recent years, however, Mata has expanded his career away from the pitch, with the player serving as a pundit at this year's World Cup for ITV, and at the 2024 European Championship for BBC Sport.

As well as appearing in the media, Mata is a keen investor in sporting ventures including Spanish club Real Oviedo, San Diego FC in the MLS and Formula One's Alpine racing team.

Alongside Italy icon Giorgio Chiellini, Mata is an investor in Mercury/13, a women's multi-club ownership group that invests in FC Como Women.

Mata is also a co-owner of Melbourne Victory, with plans to chair a football committee at the club after hanging up his boots.

As well as a shrewd businessman, Mata is also a philanthropist – and was recognised for his donations with an MBE in June 2025.

In 2017, Mata pledged one per cent of his salary to a charitable movement called Common Goal, which supports football charities.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 03:57, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 05:20.

Fighting for a spot in the top half of the Scottish Premiership, promoted St Johnstone will lock horns with in-form Falkirk at Falkirk Stadium on Saturday.

The Bairns are eyeing a sixth win on the bounce, while the Saints could go four games unbeaten this weekend.

John McGlynn's Falkirk are the form team in the Scottish top flight over the past five games, and they will be confident of earning maximum points yet again on home turf.

The latest in their string of triumphs was a 5-2 demolition of last term's runners-up Hearts at Tynecastle Park, where the Bairns raced into a 4-0 lead by the half-time interval.

Bolstering the magnitude of McGlynn's side's feat further is the fact that thrashing followed a 2-0 win against Celtic, which itself marked a third consecutive clean sheet.

All in all, taking 15 points from the last 15 on offer has put Falkirk third in the Scottish Premiership, though their 21-point tally leaves them six behind second-placed Rangers and 10 short of top-of-the-table Celtic.

On the other hand, the Bairns are now four points clear of their seventh-placed opponents, and boasting the second-best defensive record in the division, McGlynn will be optimistic about his team's chances of seeing extending that advantage.

Meanwhile, St Johnstone earned promotion to the top flight by winning the Scottish Championship last term, and while plenty of sides have struggled with the step up in the past, Simo Valakari's men are in a strong position.

The Saints are currently seventh with 17 points after 13 games, level with sixth-placed Dundee United and fifth-placed Dundee.

Prior to the international break, Valakari's side downed the Dee 2-1, taking an early lead via Josh Campbell before Kai Fotheringham won the clash roughly 20 minutes from time.

That victory ended a four-game run without a win, though St Johnstone had only tasted defeat once during that stretch, and arrive with just a single loss from their last seven outings overall.

The visitors will be the underdogs on Saturday, but buoyed by their resilience - as well as having scored more goals (17) than any other team in the bottom half - they are sure to fight for the chance to climb into the top six.

Falkirk Scottish Premiership form:.

St Johnstone Scottish Premiership form:.

Falkirk will be without injured full-backs Ryan Strain and Leon McCann, though Jack McMillan and Scott Tanser should be on hand to start either side of centre-halves Lewis Neilson and Liam Henderson.

At the opposite end of the pitch, right wingers Aodhan Doherty and Joseph Gardner are dealing with respective foot and thigh injuries, while the left-sided Ethan Laidlaw and attacking midfielder Aidan Nesbitt have ankle issues to contend with.

In their absence, Jacob Murrell looks set to start up top, supported by Ethan Ross, Finley Barbrook and Owen Eames.

As for St Johnstone, they have a generally fit squad, with centre-back Bozo Mikulic reportedly available after breaking his nose against Dundee just 14 minutes into his return from 20 months out with an ACL injury and a slew of issues in the aftermath.

Elsewhere, Joel Cotterill could operate alongside Jason Holt in the centre of the park, flanked by wing-backs Liam Smith and Josh Campbell.

Falkirk possible starting lineup:.

Bain; McMillan, Neilson, Henderson, Tanser; Spencer, Melniks; Ross, Barbrook, Eames; Murrell.

St Johnstone possible starting lineup:.

Steward; Diabate, Finlayson, Alic; Smith, Cotterill, Holt, Campbell; Steven, Schmidt, Fotheringham.

In the midst of more than just a purple patch, Falkirk have been immense of late, hammering Hearts, beating Celtic and maintaining a strong defensive record.

St Johnstone have proven their own resilience since making the step back up to the Premiership, but they will be hard-pressed to hold out against the division's form team.

#84322. Arsenal: Why Gunners and Havertz have so many offside problems

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1181 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Arsenal: Why Gunners and Havertz have so many offside problems

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:41.
  • Arsenal have built a side capable of controlling matches and turning defensive consistency into results.
  • In a recent development, according to Opta data, Arsenal have 35 offsides in the 2026-27 season, at least 11 more than any other side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:41.

Arsenal have built a side capable of controlling matches and turning defensive consistency into results. Leaders of the Premier League, with nine wins in ten games, Mikel Arteta’s team appear to have few weaknesses. There is, however, one problem that stands out: the players are caught offside with unusual frequency, and Kai Havertz is at the centre of that statistic.

In a recent development, according to Opta data, Arsenal have 35 offsides in the 2026-27 season, at least 11 more than any other side. The average of 3.5 per match is the highest for a team in a season since Hull City in 2008-09, with 3.7. The figure stands out even more when individual performance is considered: Havertz has been caught 15 times, almost double the second player in the ranking, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, with eight.

Sources indicate that the number is not just a statistical curiosity. Every offside stops a move and wastes an attacking opportunity. But the explanation does not lie in a single factor. Arsenal’s style creates situations conducive to this type of infringement, opponents also play a part in the picture and, in Havertz’s case, there is a clear problem with the timing of his movements.

The first explanation lies in how Arteta’s team occupy the pitch. Arsenal are a side that usually control possession, settle their players in the opposition half and circulate the ball until they find spaces to advance.

This territorial presence increases the number of situations in which the attackers can try to exploit the space behind the last line. When the ball reaches a player with room to lift his head, team-mates look to attack the depth, either to receive a vertical pass or to open space for those arriving from behind.

Industry observers note that it is a crucial movement for a team that frequently faces opponents in low blocks. If all the attackers waited for the ball to feet, Arsenal would have more difficulty disorganising compact defences. Attacking the space behind the centre-backs forces the opponent to make decisions: drop back to protect the area or push the line up to reduce the space between defence and midfield.

The problem is that the second alternative demands extra attention from the attackers. When the opposition defence advances in a coordinated way, the player starting the run must watch not only the ball but also the positions of the defenders. If he sets off before the pass, he can be offside even if he receives in good conditions.

According to recent reports, arsenal are third in the Premier League in ‘field tilt’, an indicator that measures the proportion of passes made in the attacking third relative to the total passes in the final thirds of the pitch, at 64.1%. They are also second for attempted through balls (31), passes ending in the attacking third (1,662) and passes that break the opposition defensive line (207).

In other words, the team create many situations in which their attackers can be found behind the defence. In addition, they have faced six of the sides that have most often caught opponents offside this season: Aston Villa, Coventry, Hull City, Leeds, Liverpool and Brighton. It is no coincidence that part of the numbers were built against opponents especially prepared to use this resource.

The high line, therefore, helps explain the problem but is not enough to justify it. Manchester City and Tottenham, for example, have higher possession and territorial dominance figures, while Brighton also surpass Arsenal in passes that break the defence. Even so, Arsenal are clear leaders in offsides. There is also a sampling factor. Arsenal were caught eight times against Aston Villa in August, the most by a side in a single Premier League match in the past two and a half years.

Sources indicate that in just ten games, such an outlying match carries considerable weight in the average. But the seven offsides against Leeds, five against Coventry and four against Hull show it is not an isolated episode.

If collective behaviour explains part of the picture, Havertz’s situation stands out for another reason. The German has 15 offsides, a figure too high to be attributed only to the style of play or the characteristics of the opponents.

There is a perception that Havertz, having played as a midfielder for much of his career, prefers to drop back to take part in build-up play. But the data show he also frequently looks to attack the space behind the defence. In the Premier League, he has made 125 high-intensity runs of this type, the third highest figure in the competition.

Gonzalo Garcia, of Fulham, made 145 of these runs and was caught offside only twice. Bryan Mbeumo, of Manchester United, made 141 and was flagged four times. Both have played at least 90 minutes more than Havertz.

This does not mean the German should stop attacking the depth. The question is the quality of execution. The attacker needs to identify the moment when his team-mate is ready to make the pass and adjust his sprint to the movement of the defence.

Industry observers note that offside can come down to centimetres. A forward who sets off too early loses the chance to receive legally, even if he has correctly identified the space. If he delays, he lets the defender recover and close the passing lane.

Some of Havertz’s moves this season look more avoidable. There are also situations in which the team need to improve collective coordination. Arsenal have had 11 offsides within 15 seconds of a set piece being taken. On two occasions, players were caught after long balls from goalkeeper David Raya. These are moves that demand attention from the attackers and better communication about when to attack the space.

So far, the offsides have not stopped Arsenal building an excellent campaign. They lead the Premier League with 27 points, five clear of second place. Defensive solidity allows the team to win matches even when the attack does not produce a high volume of goals.

Sources indicate that but there is a possible side effect. Arsenal have scored only 15 times in the first ten games. At that rate, they would finish the season with 57 goals, which would be the lowest total in the history of a Premier League champion. The team can keep winning with their defensive organisation, but will hardly have the same safety margin if their rivals improve their attacking performance.

Sources indicate that the 35 offsides represent possessions interrupted before the move could reach its end. Not all would be clear goalscoring opportunities, but some could result in dangerous shots. In a tight race, wasting so many attacks can make a difference.

Arteta’s challenge is not to ask his players to stop attacking the depth. That would mean giving up an key tool for dismantling compact defences. The way forward is to improve coordination between the passer and the runner, as well as to guide the players better on how to react to the opposition defensive line.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 – Saturday 21 November 2026 5.30pm.

If you ever wanted proof of how unpredictable football is, here is the ultimate proof.

Arsenal absolutely dominated the first half.

They looked very much like they were the reigning champions and league leaders by five points.

According to recent reports, newcastle United didn’t get a kick. Well, not a kick where it mattered.

Arsenal dominating the ball and territory, Newcastle just clearing the ball and it coming straight back at them.

Bruno Guimaraes had headed a close in header just wide and it felt like a goal was inevitable.

It has been revealed that the visitors were breaking the half-hearted United press with ease and you really had to feel for Lewis Hall when the goal did come. He didn’t deal with a ball he should have, next thing Havertz with a very clever ball that Dedic wasn’t alive to and Eze giving Hornicek no chance.

Matthias Jaissle took decisive action for the second half, with Ramsey, Elanga and Livramento replacing Steur, Murphy and Dedic.

Inside four minutes Newcastle were level.

In almost the exact same part of the pitch, Odegaard made a far worse blunder than Hall had for their goal. Osula taking advantage to feed Barnes in the box and a great low finish.

It was then all suddenly Newcastle United pouring forward and the first half seemed like another match.

Just after the hour mark an excellent corner routine saw Hall cross from the right and Burn a free header, that caused chaos and Malick Thiaw on hand to smash it home from a yard out.

Var vainly tried to find a handball, then it was looking for an offside, before admitting defeat.

Somehow, somehow, Newcastle United were now ahead!

Newcastle didn’t sit back and continued to look for another goal, absolutely the right tactics. Rather than sit back.

Arteta making subs and Bruno Guimaraes trudging off as one of them.

In a recent development, the Arsenal equaliser was a great goal for them as they played it from back to front but Newcastle could have defended it better as Madueke cut inside. Plus Hornicek should have saved it, even though the shot went through a defender’s legs.

More than twenty minutes then played including nine minutes added time, with a pretty even closing period of the match, even though you naturally adopted the stance of you just know Arsenal are going to find a winner somehow….

This was absolutely remarkable stuff.

Never in a million years did you see that second half coming after Arsenal had total control of the first.

It has been revealed that newcastle at last seeing a bit of luck going their way with that Odegaard mistake and suddenly that helped give confidence and momentum. Plus it helped that United brought on three mobile players all able to carry the ball and with a bit of pace.

No doubt the extremist Matthias Jaissle haters won’t want to give him any credit.

However, I think he was brave with his substitutions and I have a feeling that whatever 11 he had played in the first half, we would have seen Arsenal dominate the opening 45.

A hopeless first half and a second half that gives hope.

West Ham United have received a boost ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, with striker Johnny Kenny ruled out through injury. The 22-year-old has suffered a hamstring tear and is expected to remain sidelined beyond Upcoming Year’s Day.

In a recent development, preston manager Graham Alexander confirmed the extent of the injury in an interview with the Lancashire Evening Post, having lost Kenny during the defeat to Sheffield United earlier this month. The striker’s absence adds to Preston’s injury problems ahead of their visit to the London Stadium.

However, Preston have already demonstrated they can win without Kenny, having beaten Southampton in their previous fixture. Midfielder Léo Leroy is also available again after suspension, although captain Ali McCann remains sidelined.

Soungoutou Magassa was reinstated to the West Ham squad following the arrival of Parker.

Parker has already shown that he’s prepared to use Magassa, having recalled him for the Cardiff City match.

And with West Ham’s defensive problems continuing, I suspect the fresh manager will want somebody sitting in front of the defence to provide additional protection.

It’s a possibility we’ve previously discussed when examining Parker’s prepares for the international break, and the manager has now had considerably more time to work on his tactical approach.

Kenny’s absence is undoubtedly welcome news for West Ham, but it won’t dictate Parker’s team selection.

As recent training footage has demonstrated, Magassa has been involved in Parker’s preparations.

Whether that results in a starting place against Preston remains to be seen.

A heated exchange at the London Assembly has thrust West Ham United’s London Stadium back into the spotlight, with Susan Hall challenging Mayor Sadiq Khan’s Chief of Staff, David Bellamy, over the stadium’s mounting losses and the failure to secure a naming rights sponsor.

The confrontation took place during the Assembly’s Budget and Performance Committee scrutiny, with Hall questioning why a venue of such prominence continues to cost taxpayers approximately £20 million annually, according to City AM’s report.

Bellamy insisted that City Hall remains in the market for a naming rights partner, with discussions ongoing. However, he acknowledged that West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League has made securing a lucrative sponsorship agreement more difficult.

Hall has accused the Mayor of failing to deliver a sponsorship deal despite having a decade to find one.

The exchange highlights the extraordinary financial problems surrounding the former Olympic Stadium and raises fresh questions about its long-term future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 06:43 EST, 18 November 2026.

Manchester United have expressed their concern over the circumstances surrounding JJ Gabriel’s imminent move to Real Madrid, and threatened legal action if there is any evidence that he was induced to leave.

The 16-year-old winger posted a video on social media on Tuesday night confirming his departure from United as talks with Madrid continue between his newly introduced agent Ali Barat and close family at the club’s Valdebebas headquarters.

United sources say they are disappointed the video appeared without any contact with them, but the club will maintain its policy of not punishing Gabriel for what it sees as the actions of adults.

However, they have reiterated that United will fight with every legal means possible if any evidence of inducement from another club comes to light.

It has been revealed that it’s understood that United have been unable to make contact with Gabriel – who has not been seen at the club since September – or his family despite numerous attempts to check on his welfare. They want an opportunity to ensure that he has a say in what could be a life-changing decision.

Gabriel has been training in Madrid and gave an interview to Marca earlier this month saying that he favoured a move to the 15-time European champions over rivals Barcelona, while expressing an ambition to win the Ballon d’Or.

Manchester United are prepared for a legal fight with Real Madrid over JJ Gabriel.

The youngster is on the verge of joining the Spanish giants in a controversial move.

It has been revealed that he is registered as a United player for the rest of the season and the club are refusing to tear up that agreement in the belief that he would still need approval from FIFA to make the move. However, sources stress that there has been no contact from any football authority seeking to de-register him.

Gabriel has been at United since the age of 11, and is considered one of the hottest young prospects in European football. He is registered with United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.

There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.

In a farewell post on Instagram he said: 'Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with major dreams.

'Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

It has been revealed that 'You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

In a recent development, 'As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ.'.

Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.

United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered his request to leave given he had become a key part of intends in first team training sessions this season.

United were left rocked in September when Gabriel's family unexpectedly requested to cancel his contract with immediate effect.

Daily Mail Sport revealed at the time that United’s hierarchy were left unsure what triggered such a move given he had become a key part of plans in first team training sessions this season under Michael Carrick.

A week later, Daily Mail Sport revealed that the decline of United since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson was the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

'His dad has ambitions for his son to be the best in the world and play with the best and learn from the best and right now that's not current situation at United - far from it,' a source explained.

He has not been seen at the club since he scored a hat-trick for the Under 21s on his UEFA Youth League debut against Sabah.

By Lewis Blain | 20 Nov 2026 07:07.

Mauricio Pochettino is keen to make significant behind-the-scenes changes at Manchester United following his arrival at Old Trafford.

The latest Red Devils boss is understood to have identified a preferred candidate to replace sporting director Jason Wilcox, with whom he previously enjoyed a successful working relationship.

Paul Mitchell could now emerge as a leading contender for a return to football after previously being considered by INEOS.

According to reports, Pochettino has recommended Mitchell as United's next sporting director, believing the 45-year-old would be the ideal replacement for Wilcox.

The Argentine, who has signed a contract until June 2029, is said to have made his concerns about Wilcox clear during discussions with the club hierarchy before accepting the managerial position.

Wilcox has come under scrutiny following United's disappointing recent form and questions over the quality and depth of the squad assembled during his time at the club.

Pochettino is keen to work with someone he trusts, having previously enjoyed productive spells alongside Mitchell at Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur.

Mitchell was reportedly considered by INEOS for a senior football position in October 2023, before Wilcox ultimately took the role in April 2024.

Sources indicate that the 45-year-old recruitment chief also held positions at RB Leipzig and Monaco before spending 11 months as Newcastle's sporting director between 2024 and 2025. He has been out of football since departing St James' Park.

There are legitimate questions over whether Wilcox has delivered enough to justify remaining in such an influential position at Old Trafford.

United's summer recruitment has left several important areas of the squad needing attention, particularly left-back and centre-forward, while the club have also struggled to generate funds by moving on unwanted players.

Marcus Rashford's situation is one example of the wider challenge of moving players who no longer fit the club's plans.

Furthermore, the decision to appoint Michael Carrick permanently before his eventual departure will inevitably come under scrutiny, especially given the responsibility placed on the sporting department to identify the right managerial appointment.

Mitchell would bring considerable recruitment experience and, crucially, an existing relationship with Pochettino.

INEOS should not make a change simply to satisfy a latest manager, but if Wilcox has failed to provide the squad-building structure and recruitment strategy United need, replacing him could be a sensible step.

Pochettino needs a sporting director who shares his vision, and Mitchell could be a compelling candidate to help deliver that.

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

Recent findings suggest that “Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

Sources indicate that “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

Sources indicate that the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Industry observers note that major? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

According to recent reports, leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

According to recent reports, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

According to recent reports, ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

According to recent reports, A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

It has been revealed that “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

Sources indicate that it’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Recent findings suggest that exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

According to recent reports, for each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

It has been revealed that energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

According to recent reports, there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Sources indicate that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the fresh boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

It has been revealed that the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

It has been revealed that newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Recent findings suggest that joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who indicates that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the Newly introduced Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United v Preston North End EFL Championship London Stadium Saturday 21 November 2026, 3pm GMT.

Industry observers note that scott Parker’s first home match as West Ham United head coach is massively key. Preston North End are bottom of the Championship and, while Saturday’s fixture is not mathematically must-win, realistically it feels very close to it.

West Ham have collected one point from Parker’s opening two games and must start closing the gap to the automatic-promotion places. After two uninterrupted weeks with much of his squad, this is the first proper opportunity to judge whether the new head coach has begun improving the organisation and intensity of the team.

In a recent development, there is also the troubling matter of West Ham’s home form. I worried before relegation that the vast gaps between the London Stadium crowd and the pitch might turn it into a disadvantage rather than an advantage, and we now desperately need to begin winning there consistently.

The London Stadium has not remotely resembled a fortress this season. Opponents have arrived believing they can frustrate West Ham, exploit the anxiety around the ground and capitalise when the players become nervous.

As one former Championship striker recently observed, visiting teams have been enjoying the London Stadium experience. That situation has to change if West Ham are serious about challenging for automatic promotion.

It has been revealed that parker needs his players to begin rapidly and give the crowd something to respond to. The longer this remains goalless, the more Preston will believe their long-ball approach and deep defensive shape can earn them something.

Scott Parker will need to make the London Stadium feel like home.

West Ham will dominate possession, so the challenge will be using it properly. Passing sideways in front of an organised defence will achieve very little; we need quicker movement, runners beyond the striker and enough tempo to pull Preston out of position.

Recent findings suggest that I expect West Ham to be considerably tighter defensively following Parker’s first extended spell on the training pitch. However, the international break has not been quite as useful as it initially appeared because several vital players were away representing their countries.

Industry observers note that konstantinos Mavropanos was among those absent, while Max Kilman is suspended after reaching the disciplinary threshold at Blackburn. Parker has therefore been unable to work throughout the fortnight with the central-defensive partnership he will need on Saturday.

I suspect Morato will move into his natural centre-back position alongside Mavropanos. That is probably the safe and predictable selection, although I would prefer to see Airidas Golambeckis given the opportunity.

The teenager has generally impressed when called upon and deserves serious consideration. As our examination of Parker’s defensive conundrum against Preston highlighted, the decision appears to be between Morato’s experience and Golambeckis’ encouraging performances.

According to recent reports, joël Veltman should start at right-back, while Ezra Mayers deserves to retain his place on the left. Kyle Walker-Peters continues to be assessed, but Parker has two natural and capable full-back options without needing to rush him back.

The biggest selection question surrounds the goalkeeper. I am finding Parker’s team difficult to predict primarily because I do not know whether he will retain Mads Hermansen or turn to Alphonse Areola.

Recent findings suggest that hermansen has produced an inconsistent sequence of performances. He excelled for Denmark against Portugal before making another clanger during the defeat by Norway, which will not have made Parker’s decision any easier.

According to recent reports, there has been considerable pressure for West Ham to make a change in goal, but Areola’s own fitness has reportedly been an problem. Until Parker confirms otherwise, my best guess is that Hermansen will retain his place.

I suspect Parker will stick with Hermansen.

Industry observers note that this is an ideal fixture in which to rebuild the goalkeeper’s confidence, but Preston’s likely use of long balls and set pieces means he must command his penalty area properly. Another nervous display would only intensify the debate but my own choice would be to select Finn Herrick.

Sources indicate that I expect Parker to continue with the 4-2-3-1 formation. Arne Engels and Soungoutou Magassa should form the central-midfield partnership, with Divine Mukasa operating further forward.

It has been revealed that magassa gives West Ham a recognised holding midfielder and should help protect a changed defence. That will allow Engels to move the ball forward and support Mukasa rather than both central midfielders occupying similar positions.

In a recent development, preston’s victory over Southampton was built around an aggressive pressing approach, something Parker will have worked on during the break. I previously argued that West Ham must learn to play through Preston’s press, and this midfield should contain enough composure and energy to do it.

Industry observers note that jarrod Bowen will naturally start on the right, with Edvin Austbø on the left. In my opinion, Austbø has moved ahead of Manor Solomon in the pecking order and deserves a proper run in the team.

In a recent development, joël Piroe should lead the attack. Parker needs to give West Ham’s most proven Championship goalscorer an extended opportunity rather than continually rotating strikers who have struggled to find any rhythm.

I expect five players who were away on international duty—Hermansen, Mavropanos, Mukasa, Austbø and Piroe—to start. The key defensive change should see Morato move inside to replace the suspended Kilman.

Industry observers note that preston earned their first victory under Graham Alexander by beating Southampton before the international break, so they should arrive with renewed confidence. However, both of their Championship wins this season have come at home.

Their away record is dreadful. Preston are winless on the road, having drawn once and lost six of their seven away league matches, including some heavy defeats.

It has been revealed that I expect them to use plenty of long balls, remain compact and try to frustrate West Ham. Even so, the Hammers have far better players and will enjoy the lion’s share of possession.

According to recent reports, quite frankly, it is time they highlighted the difference in quality. If West Ham cannot beat the Championship’s bottom club at home after Parker has been given two weeks to prepare, serious questions will remain about our promotion credentials.

It has been revealed that preston may make the opening stages awkward, but West Ham should eventually have far too much attacking quality. Parker’s team need to play with intensity, move the ball quickly and turn possession into genuine chances rather than merely dominating the statistics.

I expect a much more organised performance following the international break. Preston’s direct approach may still produce a goal, particularly with West Ham fielding a changed central defence, but this should be the afternoon Parker claims his first victory.

Prediction: West Ham United 4-1 Preston North End.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta watched on as his Arsenal team dominated Newcastle United in the first half.

United fortunate to be only one down after the opening half.

A completely different second half though, Newcastle United by far the better team and Arsenal lucky in the end to grab a point.

Arsenal going six points clear but Brighton with a game in hand.

So what did Mikel Arteta make of it all?

According to recent reports, mikel Arteta asked about Bruno Guimaraes making an emotional return to St James’ Park and how he thought he dealt with it: “Very good. We spoke about that before the game. Because inevitably, emotionally, you have so much going on, especially in the way that he feels connected to this club, having been the captain and everything that they did together. But I think he was very composed and he was very, very, very focused on what he had to do in the game. I think for the time that he was on the pitch he had a really good performance.”.

Suggested to Mikel Arteta that a point at St James’ Park is usually a good result but that he won’t feel like that is the case tonight: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. We were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. The intensity, the level of aggression, the intensity that we put on the defensive aspects, the quality that we demonstrated. Thee clarity to understand the jobs, the composure that we have with the ball, the aggressiveness that we have to attack the right spaces, we should have been two, three, or four up clearly. When you don’t do that then the opponent is going to try to react, we play at the same level but we still have to increase the level to cope with that. Then right at the beginning of the second half we aren’t at the races, we start to lose duels, we start to lose second balls, we give the ball away, really poor circulation goals against their press and their waves. When that happens, you give them belief. One thing is to give them belief, and another thing is to give them a goal. We give them a goal from a throw, that is obviously very, very, very disappointing. On top of that we give them a corner, we give them the best player that they have on the pitch on set-pieces free.”.

It has been revealed that mikel Arteta on Newcastle United and the fans: “You have to give credit to Newcastle United as well for that period of time [when they were on top], the quality, the aggression, the conviction that they showed that they could get back in the game. The same with the stadium, which we know that when it comes to these evenings, they believe that they can do it, it’s another push. We have won football matches playing much worse than we have done here. But it is not enough because when the margins are so small, everything matters.”.

By Sebastian Sternik | 20 Nov 2026 07:20.

Union Berlin are in the midst of their second-worst start to a Bundesliga season, and things are not about to get any easier as the relegation contenders prepare to host an in-form RB Leipzig side this Saturday afternoon.

While Die Eisernen are languishing in the bottom three, Die Roten Bullen are eyeing up a fourth straight league victory as they continue to chase the Bundesliga’s top two.

With just seven points to their name from their opening nine Bundesliga matches, Union Berlin are already feeling the pressure.

Head coach Mauro Lustrinelli survived the international break, with the club's hierarchy seemingly prepared to give the Swiss tactician more time to turn things around.

However, his long-term future remains far from certain, particularly after director Horst Heldt cast doubt over whether the 47-year-old would still be in charge over the next five months.

Heldt also revealed that Union are already drawing up aims for the January transfer window, although with more than a month to go before it opens, any potential reinforcements are unlikely to provide Lustrinelli with immediate relief.

What may help the Swiss coach is the fact Union’s best results this season have come at home, with 86% of all their points coming at the Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Nevertheless, Union's defensive problems overshadow any slight positives, given they have already conceded 21 goals - a latest club record at this stage of a Bundesliga campaign.

While Union struggle to keep the ball out of the net, RB Leipzig simply cannot stop scoring at the moment.

Martin Demichelis and his men have already rattled the net 27 times in the Bundesliga this season - a total only bettered by Bayern Munich, who have scored on 29 occasions.

Just before the international break, Leipzig put five goals past Augsburg in a 5-2 victory - a game which extended their winning run to three straight league matches.

In recent times, Leipzig have also seen an upswing in their away results, winning their last two competitive games on the road - including a 2-0 success against Schalke at the end of October.

Striking early has been the key for Die Rotten Bullen so far this season, with the club yet to drop a point when scoring first in the Bundesliga.

In fact, the only major concern ahead of Saturday’s game is the fact Leipzig have lost four of their last six trips to Stadion An der Alten Forsterei.

Union Berlin form (all competitions):.

RB Leipzig form (all competitions):.

French defender Stanley Nsoki has missed every game this season for Union Berlin due to a muscle injury, and the 27-year-old will remain on the sidelines this weekend.

Robert Skov has only played one competitive minute this term, though he has recently returned to individual training.

Youngster Andrik Markgraf also remains out of action due to a knee injury, while Janik Haberer could miss Saturday’s game through illness.

When it comes to RB Leipzig, the visitors are also dealing with a handful of injuries as we head towards the end of the calendar year.

German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo has been out of action since September with a shoulder problem.

Youngsters Viggo Gebel and Marc Guiu are also dealing with knee and hamstring injuries.

Max Finkgrafe, meanwhile, has missed his last five games with a thigh injury, but is on the brink of a return.

Antonio Nusa, who has 11 goal contributions in nine Bundesliga games this season, is the man to watch for the visitors.

Union Berlin possible starting lineup:.

Ronnow; Juranovic, Van den Bosch, Friedrich, Rothe; Imeri, Schafer, Khedira, Aebischer; Ilic, Burke.

RB Leipzig possible starting lineup:.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; El Aynaoui, Banzuzi; Gruda, Nkunku, Nusa; Romulo.

Union Berlin perform a lot better at home, but that may not be enough to stop a rampant RB Leipzig side that simply cannot stop scoring goals.

The visitors smell blood as they continue to chase the top two, and there is a strong possibility that things could get ugly in Berlin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham United midfielder Arne Engels is attracting interest from Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart, although the German club could struggle to afford the £22m summer signing.

Industry observers note that according to German newspaper BILD, as reported by Sport Witness, Stuttgart have identified Engels as one of several potential replacements for Angelo Stiller, who could leave the club next summer. Southampton’s Caspar Jander and Middlesbrough’s Aidan Morris are also under consideration.

Recent findings suggest that however, Stuttgart reportedly regard the cost of signing Engels as unrealistic, with West Ham unlikely to accept a substantial loss on a player who only arrived from Celtic in August. The German club previously wanted the Belgian during his time at Augsburg, so this is not an entirely new interest.

Look, clearly Engels is somebody that West Ham head of recruitment Nils Koppen values extremely highly.

As we reported when the £22m agreement with Celtic was reached, the Belgian had been Koppen’s primary midfield target throughout much of the summer. West Ham pursued him for weeks before finally getting their man.

I thought very quickly he’d become one of the first names on the team sheet under Nuno Espírito Santo, and I suspect that will continue under Scott Parker.

So clearly he is a player who is admired.

That remarked, I’m not surprised Stuttgart are struggling to find value at £22m because I do think West Ham overpaid when we bought him from Celtic.

West Ham midfielders will play with more freedom under Parker which could unlock Engels value.

In a recent development, now, that price becomes fully justified if he helps get the team promoted this season. If not, then I’d have to say that so far he’s done little to justify the price tag.

Industry observers note that that’s not to suggest Engels is a bad player. He’s a busy, high-energy midfielder who covers plenty of ground and contributes to the team’s overall play.

But there’s a difference between being a good Championship midfielder and looking like a £22m player.

Indeed, when I recently assessed Koppen’s summer recruitment, Engels was one of the players I felt remained something of an unknown quantity in terms of value for money.

But, and here’s the important thing, West Ham manager Scott Parker has a habit of getting central midfielders scoring goals.

And if he can get Engels further up the pitch than Nuno Espírito Santo managed to, and into goalscoring positions, I suspect his value will rise if he becomes a goalscorer rather than just a busy, high-energy midfield player.

We’ve already had a glimpse of what might be possible.

Engels scored his first West Ham goal during the extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City in Parker’s opening match, as the Hammers recovered from three goals down at half-time.

That was one of the positives from a remarkable second-half performance, which I discussed in my player ratings following the Cardiff comeback.

However, against Blackburn, Parker used Engels in a deeper midfield role, with Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa operating further forward. As our Blackburn match report highlighted, that arrangement helped protect the defence but offered Engels fewer opportunities to get forward.

It will be interesting to see whether Parker can find a balance between the two.

Engels has the energy to get around the pitch, and if he can add regular goals to his game, the argument over whether West Ham paid too much could begin to look very different.

For now, Stuttgart’s interest looks more like an indication of Engels’ standing in the game than an immediate threat to West Ham.

The Belgian is under contract until 2031, with the club holding an option for another year, as confirmed by West Ham’s official website.

And with the Hammers attempting to win promotion at the first attempt, I can’t imagine Koppen being particularly enthusiastic about losing the player he worked so hard to sign.

Personally, I still believe £22m was too much money for what Engels has shown us so far.

But if Parker can turn him into a midfielder who regularly arrives in the penalty area and contributes goals, that assessment could change considerably.

And if those goals help West Ham get promoted, nobody will be complaining about the transfer fee.

Aston Villa have been told their Champions League clash with Galatasaray on Tuesday will still take place at the home of the Turkish champions despite the worrying state of the pitch.

Galatasaray have switched their home league fixture against Samsunspor this weekend to the stadium of top-flight rivals Istanbul Basaksehir to save the playing surface from further punishment.

Images released this week show a pitch that appears to be in alarming condition, with Galatasaray working around the clock to ensure it is playable. The club are in dialogue with UEFA.

At this stage, Daily Mail Sport understands UEFA are satisfied that the pitch will be in suitable condition when the sides take the field, though a pitch inspection will take place at 10am local time as is the case before any European fixture.

UEFA Article 5 states: ‘The field of play must be smooth and level and comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game.’.

Villa will look to strengthen their position in the league phase after winning three of their opening four games, though they lost their last fixture, at Barcelona.

Galatasaray are working around the clock to ensure their pitch is up to standard for their Champions League clash against Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Unai Emery’s men have already beaten Turkish opposition this term, thrashing Fenerbahce 6-0 for their record European win, though that fixture was at Villa Park.

After the chaotic 4-4 draw at Manchester United before the international break, Villa meet Sunderland at home in the Premier League on Saturday.

Emery has doubts over Matty Cash and Johan Manzambi, who picked up injuries while on international duty and may struggle to recover in time.

West Ham United manager Scott Parker has admitted that Alphonse Areola is unlikely to be available for Saturday’s Championship clash with Preston North End, leaving the Hammers with a familiar goalkeeping dilemma.

Speaking during his pre-match press conference, Parker explained that the club had attempted to push the Frenchman’s recovery but were struggling to get him ready.

“We tried to push it a bit, but it looks a little bit unlikely and we’ll leave it as long as we can before making a decision,” mentioned the West Ham boss.

This isn’t particularly surprising. It’s something we’ve discussed previously on Claret & Hugh, with concerns surrounding Areola’s match fitness and reports that he has been carrying too much weight.

And considering Parker has worked with the Frenchman before, one has to assume he’d be really keen to play him.

The fact that he isn’t selecting Areola suggests the goalkeeper simply isn’t ready for action, particularly following his recent injury setback.

Personally, my choice would be to give young Fin Herrick a chance.

I was speaking to my Hammers Chat counterpart Geo during our West Ham v Preston preview this week, and he made an excellent observation.

The one thing Mads Hermansen has consistently been good at is his distribution with the ball at his feet.

Unfortunately, his clanger for Denmark in their last game means even that aspect of his performances is now under scrutiny.

He’s got the yips: West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, whose recent performances have raised concerns about his confidence.

I actually think the best thing we could possibly do for Hermansen would be to give him a rest.

His confidence has clearly taken a battering, and his latest international mistake has only increased the pressure.

Let’s be fair, young Herrick can’t perform any worse than the Danish keeper has in the last few games.

And as our recent coverage of supporters’ goalkeeping preferences demonstrated, there is already considerable dissatisfaction with the current situation.

I appreciate throwing a youngster into such an important game carries risks, but there comes a point when continuing with an out-of-form goalkeeper becomes an equally significant gamble.

For me, Saturday presents an opportunity to try something different.
