In a recent development, they scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

According to recent reports, it could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, indicated this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

“I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

In a recent development, THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

In a recent development, rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

In a recent development, big save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Industry observers note that the miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

In a recent development, for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

“I see him training every day,” Iraola mentioned. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he shows is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

In a recent development, is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a newly introduced contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he showed two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

His mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Recent findings suggest that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

Industry observers note that from that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some crucial saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo stated.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

“I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola noted. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is upcoming, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

It has been revealed that tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have significant confidence in my players, they are very good players.

Industry observers note that “We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

It has been revealed that unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times.

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

If left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

Recent findings suggest that 'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s rejuvenated striker Joel Piroe, fresh from a successful international break with Suriname, could hardly have picked a better opponent to face as West Ham prepare to resume their Championship campaign against Preston North End tomorrow and the Hammers’ on-loan striker seeks a return to front line duties under new boss Scott Parker.

Piroe hasn’t featured regularly under Nuno and he will be hoping for a change of fortunes under the Hammers’ upcoming head coach: The Dutch-born Suriname striker has something of a happy history against Saturday’s visitors, having scored four goals in eight previous appearances against the Lilywhites.

Proving he’s bang in form, Piroe’s two goals for Suriname last week will surely give Scott Parker the nudge needed to promoting him ahead of Taty Castellanos into the starting eleven.

The former Leeds striker has demonstrated his ability to find the net in the Championship, unlike West Ham’s often-moody Argentine forward who has but one goal to his name this season in what can only be seen as a massive disappointment.

For a side desperate to build some momentum, a striker returning from international duty with two goals under his belt and a proven record against tomorrow’s opponents can’t be overlooked.

Opportunity knocks – if Piroe can extend his Preston scoring record tomorrow he could cement a place in the starting eleven for the rest of the year. Most fans – me included – have lost patience with Taty Castellanos who doesn’t seem inclined to influence games – time for Piroe to show what he can do in an extended run in the team.

Five of Burnley's seven Championship games at Turf Moor this season have ended in draws, but they remain the only team in the division without a home victory.

As for Blackburn, they have an interim management team in place after Tony Mowbray stood down from his position earlier this week due to health challenges.

Rovers sit 11 points above their fierce rivals in the standings, the pre-season expectation having been that the points difference would be close to the exact opposite at this stage of the campaign.

In a recent development, there have been two weeks of no football and only fine words by which to judge Scott Parker’s latest era at West Ham. Well received, the new manager has expressed himself eloquently in terms that supporters will love. However, this is the fifth manager in three years to come through the doors at London Stadium and each one has spoken with well-judged words.

This is the first game in which Parker’s work to date will be judged by West Ham’s home supporters.

Fans have ‘fresh manager fatigue’ – if there is such a thing. Those players who have been at the club for three years probably the same.

It has been revealed that there’ll be an expectancy that those ‘fine words’ of Parker and Noble are turned into action on the pitch. As Mark Carlaw, writing on thewesthamway.com put it “It feels like our club is in good hands again” ..But there have been so many false dawns and fine words with the appointments of Lopetegui, Potter and Nuno all failing in their own unique ways to deliver the club from its tailspin towards mediocrity that judgement will be suspended until well after 5pm this afternoon.

“Pure grit, determination that I feel West Ham should have……….

it’s about effort, aggressiveness, a way of playing, and a real identity in a team that the fans can relate to.”.

Mark Noble’s own honest summary nailed it, so it’s time today time to see how our fresh boss is getting on in instilling this into the same bunch of players that just let in fourteen goals in the previous five games. So forgive us, Scotty P, if we hope for the best but prepare for the worst, just in case. Because this is West Ham after all. We know how this can go.

As John Cleese’s character famously put it in ‘Clockwise’:.

“Its not the despair.. I can take the despair.. it’s the hope I can’t stand”.

Legendary commentator MARTIN TYLER on taking the Premier League plunge in 1992, Arsene Wenger's fury, his love of Woking - and THAT Sergio Aguero moment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1429 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s newly introduced home or at least they will when everything is in order.
  • Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s newly introduced home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the latest satellite channel.

'A new frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

It has been revealed that 'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a big town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

In a recent development, 'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

According to recent reports, 'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

In a recent development, the Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always said you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he indicates, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he says. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

His manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s company is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

And he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' states Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' notes Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he states. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

The range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

Sources indicate that it is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 10:33, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 10:33.

Industry observers note that after losing two continental finals in the last two years, Atletico Mineiro will look to change that story this Saturday, November 21, against Boca Juniors in the Copa Sudamericana final at the Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in Barranquilla. Atletico Mineiro are chasing their first title in the competition, while the Argentines are aiming for a third following triumphs in 2004 and 2005.

Sources indicate that eduardo Dominguez’s side arrive winless in seven games and must rediscover the attacking output that underpinned their run through the tournament. Boca Juniors, under Rodolfo Arruabarrena, have won their last six matches, four of them without conceding, and head into the final in considerably better form, one that also carries a place in the 2027 Copa Libertadores group stage and the next Recopa Sudamericana.

Atletico Mineiro built their Copa Sudamericana campaign on six wins, two draws and four defeats, scoring 18 goals and conceding 14. Topping Group B secured a direct route into the last 16.

Recent findings suggest that in the knockout rounds, Atletico Mineiro faced contrasting scenarios. They eliminated RB Bragantino 3-2 on aggregate, fought back in Belo Horizonte after losing the first leg to Santos, and confirmed their place on penalties following a dramatic tie.

The semi-final again highlighted that inconsistency. Atletico Mineiro built a 3-0 lead over Montevideo City Torque at the Arena MRV and, despite losing 2-0 in Uruguay, held on to progress thanks to the cushion from the first leg.

The main concern is recent form. Since their last Brasileirao win, Atletico Mineiro have picked up five defeats and two draws, scored just three goals in that spell, and failed to find the net in five of those seven matches.

Recent findings suggest that that slump adds to the emotional weight of the two continental finals Atletico Mineiro have already lost in recent seasons, to Botafogo in the 2024 Copa Libertadores and to Lanus in the 2025 Copa Sudamericana. In another final, how the squad handles that pressure could have a direct bearing on their performance.

Sources indicate that their continental record against Argentine opposition, however, offers a point of confidence. Atletico Mineiro have not lost in regulation time to a side from the country in 14 official matches, with nine wins and five draws, a record Dominguez is likely to draw on to lift his squad in the pursuit of the title.

Recent findings suggest that boca Juniors dropped into the Copa Sudamericana after finishing third in their Copa Libertadores group. Since then, they have rebuilt their campaign, winning five, drawing one and losing two in the knockout phase, scoring 13 goals and conceding just five.

Their run began with a penalty-shootout win over O’Higgins and gained momentum in the last 16, when they beat Recoleta home and away. In the quarter-finals, they managed the advantage built at home and eliminated Sao Paulo with a draw in Brazil.

Sources indicate that the semi-final demanded a stronger response. Having been beaten by Vasco da Gama at La Bombonera, Boca Juniors turned the tie around at the Maracana, showing they could raise their level when needing a result away from home.

Recent form backs up that improvement. Boca Juniors have won six matches in a row across all competitions, scoring 11 goals and conceding just two, a run that combines sharper finishing with a more settled defence. They also arrive on the back of the Liga Argentina title, secured with a stoppage-time Enner Valencia goal in a win over Defensa y Justicia on November 7.

Against Brazilian sides in continental competition in 2026, Boca Juniors have two wins, two draws and two defeats, with six goals scored and five conceded. In the overall head-to-head, the Argentines hold the edge, but Atletico Mineiro have won the two most recent knockout meetings between the clubs, adding some balance to the final’s history.

Sources indicate that lyanco has returned to training but remains a doubt after missing the last two games. Fred, Ruan and Cassierra have already come back and featured against Mirassol, while Bernard remains one of the side’s main attacking outlets in the competition.

Sources indicate that at Boca Juniors, Agustin Marchesin is out with a knee ligament injury and was not even registered for the competition, although he has travelled with the squad. Rodrigo Battaglia has also returned to training with the group, widening Arruabarrena’s options. In attack, Tomas Aranda is competing with Alan Velasco and Leonel Flores, with no official word yet on who will complete the forward line alongside Sebastian Villa and Miguel Merentiel.

Boca Juniors possible starting lineup:.

Boca Juniors arrive in the more solid moment and have shown greater composure in controlling matches. If they can impose their rhythm, they stand to exploit the difficulties Atletico Mineiro have had reacting under pressure.

It has been revealed that atletico Mineiro still have the quality to cause problems, but the dip in form and the fitness doubts narrow their margin for error. The projection, therefore, is for a narrow Boca Juniors win, in a tight final likely to be decided by small details.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 11:19.

Roma have reportedly identified Nottingham Forest winger Callum Hudson-Odoi as a potential transfer target.

Despite recent capitulations in the Champions League, Roma sit in third position in the Serie A table.

With 31 goals scored in 10 matches, Gian Piero Gasperini's side boast the best attacking record in Italy's top flight.

Nevertheless, Roma continue to be linked with attacking additions during the winter market, with Chelsea wide man Jamie Gittens known to be a long-term target.

While Corriere dello Sport reiterates that stance on the England Under-21 international, it appears that Hudson-Odoi could also be targeted by the Italian giants.

The report suggests that Hudson-Odoi has been placed on Roma's shortlist of wingers, albeit below Gittens.

Although he was viewed as a key player under previous Forest managers, Hudson-Odoi is yet to make a start since the arrival of Oliver Glasner.

He has accumulated just 76 minutes of football across five substitute appearances in all competitions.

While the 26-year-old has a contract in place until 2028, it appears increasingly plausible that he could depart the City Ground during the next window.

As a result of Forest only committing to a deal in the region of £5m when signing Hudson-Odoi from Chelsea, there could be opportunities to make a substantial profit.

Hudson-Odoi has contributed 19 goals and 10 assists from his 118 appearances for Forest.

With regards to Gittens, Roma will not be able to afford Chelsea's valuation of a player who cost at least £48.5m in the summer of 2025.

Therefore, Roma will realistically only look to sign the 22-year-old on a loan deal until the end of 2026-27.

However, if Forest are prepared to cash in on Hudson-Odoi for a fee in the region of £10m and still double their money on the player, Roma could plausibly consider signing him on a permanent basis.

That remarked, Forest may be able to generate a sizeable loan fee for Hudson-Odoi and still sell him for a fee in the 2027 summer transfer window.

#84256. Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2,3,4,5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep’s wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

As we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has big looks to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The latest ‘MSE’ holding company is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

Sources indicate that serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

“You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

In a recent development, “So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

Recent findings suggest that “This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

“Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

“The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

Recent findings suggest that “This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

“Building a great stadium like this is something extremely important. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this organization that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

Industry observers note that “So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this newly introduced stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this new stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European firm – but I would also say worldwide.

According to recent reports, “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the fresh stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 11:28, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 11:47.

England will play Norway in the quarter-finals of the UEFA Nations League.

The Three Lions progressed to the last eight as League A Group 3 winners, having collected 15 points from six matches, including a sensational 3-2 win over Spain on the final matchday.

England's first-placed status meant that they entered the draw as one of the four seeded quarter-finalists, alongside France, Germany and Portugal, while they were unable to be drawn against Spain having already faced them in the group stage.

Thomas Tuchel's side will therefore do battle with Erling Haaland's Norway, who finished as runners-up to Portugal in League A Group 4 and will be seeking revenge for their World Cup 2026 quarter-final defeat to England.

Should England prevail in their reunion with the Scandinavians, they will clash with either Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals, for the right to contest a heavyweight showpiece event.

Industry observers note that ?????????? Thomas Tuchel's #ThreeLions will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March! https://t.co/TQBDCd9I4i.

The headline quarter-final sees reigning world and European champions Spain square off with France, a repeat of the 2020-21 Nations League final which Les Bleus won 2-1.

Whoever wins that clash of the titans will pit their wits against either the Netherlands or Portugal, who also squared off in the final of the inaugural Nations League in 2019; the Selecao triumphed 1-0 thanks to a Goncalo Guedes strike.

The first legs of the Nations League quarter-finals will take place between March 25 and March 27, before the return fixtures are held across March 28 and March 30.

Recent findings suggest that england will travel to Norway for their first clash, before welcoming the Nordic nation to Wembley for the return fixture. The semi-finals and final will then be held in June in an as yet undetermined host nation.

Meanwhile, the Republic of Ireland will take on Croatia in the League A/League B playoffs for the right to earn promotion to the top tier, while Wales must beat Slovenia to retain their League A status.

Wales finished bottom of League A Group 4 on three points, but survived automatic relegation to the second division thanks to their superior points total to Turkey and the Czech Republic (both 0).

The Dragons have only ever faced Slovenia once before, drawing 0-0 in a 2005 international friendly.

Ireland's runners-up finish in League B Group 3 means that they have the chance to rise to League A for the first time ever, having only competed in League B since the Nations League's inception.

The Boys in Green have only beaten Croatia twice in their previous seven meetings, though, and lost 3-1 during their most recent head-to-head at Euro 2012.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

It has been revealed that kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick stated. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

According to recent reports, erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

According to recent reports, “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick mentioned. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a massive game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

According to recent reports, “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win swiftly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Sources indicate that mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Recent findings suggest that gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react swiftly enough.

In a recent development, “It’s been really, really tough, going through the months not playing, not being in the squad. It was a case of making sure I stick at it and having the mentality to come in every day and still improve and perform when I couldn’t really see any opportunities coming my way.

“I’ve been given an opportunity now and it’s been really good. The world works for you sometimes and I’m definitely going to give it my all and stake my claim to become a part of the team.”.

One of several young, talented players who’d become invisible under Nuno – Scarles and Ajala included – Ezra Mayers serves as a brilliant example of one who didn’t let his standards slip even whilst out of the team and the reckoning.

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 12:42.

With ten representatives at The Under-17 World in Qatar, Africa has several promising generations, with players already noticed at the last Africa Cup of Nations and graduates of prestigious academies. Here are five profiles to watch closely, who could use this event to move up a level.

Some are already considered major figures in their national teams, while others will have the chance to make a name for themselves with the general public and recruiters.

Morocco have several interesting individuals, but Ibrahim Rabbaj is already considered the star of the team. Born in England, the 17-year-old forward plays for Chelsea, where he has gradually climbed the ranks until joining the Under-18 group. Creative, technical and able to play both centrally and on the flank, he has a fine attacking palette. Versatile, he has even occasionally filled in as a left-back at club level!

Industry observers note that already crowned African Under-17 champion with Morocco in 2025, he has been able to gauge the demands of major competitions. Under former international Ahmed Kantari, he will have the chance to confirm that his potential can also be expressed on the world stage.

Algeria return to the Under-17 World Cup for the first time since 2009 and will be able to count on Yacine Abed to lead their attack.

Trained at Paradou AC, the most prolific academy in the country, the forward particularly stood out at the last Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, where he notably scored twice against South Africa (2-0), helping Algeria’s youngsters take a big step towards qualification.

Quick and technical, Abed has an interesting profile to unsettle opposing defences. This World Cup will be an opportunity to confirm his promise against opposition of a different calibre.

Interesting transfer as Ivorian youth international Harafat Diabaté (2009) ?? has committed to join Celta Vigo, officially signing next January. More on him soon! ? https://t.co/yyhc0ZdCsK.

In a recent development, for Ivory Coast, Mohamed Harafat Diabate is a name to remember. The Celta Vigo forward, who joined in July from Racing Club d’Abidjan, could use this competition to make himself stand out. He had already caught the eye at the Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, notably scoring the winning penalty against DR Congo (1-0) in the final minutes of the match.

It has been revealed that alongside players such as Hubert Yao Kouassi, he represents an additional option for an Ivorian side that is not short of ambition. His ability to be decisive in key moments will be watched particularly closely in Qatar.

Recent findings suggest that reigning African champions, Senegal have a particularly interesting generation. Among their talents, El Hadji Ibrahima Sow deserves particular attention. A product of AS Dakar Sacre-Coeur, which has produced Pathe Mboup, Alassane Ndao and Iliman Ndiaye, the attacking midfielder is already playing in the Senegalese top flight despite being 16.

Recent findings suggest that his main quality is his vision of the game. Able to find spaces between the lines, deliver passes in the final metres and pose a threat from set pieces, Sow has the profile of a true playmaker. His intelligence and calm in decisive areas could help Senegal, who dream of taking another step after their continental triumph.

It has been revealed that finally, Cameroon will be able to count on Douka Nkoto, a midfielder in the Manchester United academy. Initially trained in Cameroon, at Player FC of Yaounde, he joined the Manchester United academy with his brother Bassirou. Although born in Cameroon, he had started out representing England before being brought back into the Cameroon fold through a step up to the Under-23 side, alongside his brother.

The two players, both born in 2010, are presented as modern midfielders, able to put in repeated efforts, win the ball back and push forward. Douka will notably need to show his ability to manage the rhythm and intensity of an international competition. For Cameroon, who have never yet got past the group stage of an Under-17 World Cup, his contribution in midfield could be valuable.

  • The first line up of the Scott Parker era has been confirmed: And there’s a couple of major shocks with third choice keeper Fin Herrick selected in place of Mads Hermansen AND Edson Alvarez getting a recall!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Preston North End at home – and a traditional 3pm kick off on a Saturday afternoon is Scott Parker’s home debut as West Ham United manager. The expectation is high after many fine words from fan favourites Parker and his assistant Mark Noble – and of course the two week break from football has only heightened the anticipation as bottom club Preston come to visit.

In a recent development, after beginning with a draw and a loss within his first three days at the helm, Parker gets to show us ‘his’ West Ham line up and set up this afternoon. Having had a two week break to work with the bulk of his West Ham side, we’ll get to see a Scott Parker XI now along with the manner in which he aims to set his team up.

The first line up of the Scott Parker era has been confirmed: And there’s a couple of major shocks with third choice keeper Fin Herrick selected in place of Mads Hermansen AND Edson Alvarez getting a recall!

Herrick | Veltman, Mavropanos, Morato, Mayers | Engels Alvarez Mukasa | Bowen, Piroe, Austbo.

Unsurprisingly we’re all in the upbeat and full of hope camp: – especially after seeing that line up.

The game is not televised so why not join the Hammers chat watch along on YouTube? Audio coverage is on BBC Radio London and we’ll be backwash player ratings as soon as the final whistle is blown.

Breaking: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1,2,3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a fresh and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

a,b, The reconstructed 5° twisted interface maximizes Ti coordination in b compared with the rigid structure in a. This reconstruction favours fully coordinated Ti sites (CN = 6, pink and beige) by minimizing undercoordinated Ti regions (CN = 5, yellow and green). This induces a dislocation (shaded grey region) between the two undercoordinated stackings. The insets on the right depict atomic positions across the interface for a central unit cell, illustrating the coordination environment.

Unit-cell averaged εxx, εyy and εxy (from left to right) using the described nearest-neighbour scheme for the TiO2-terminated and SrO-terminated layers (from top to bottom, respectively).

Industry observers note that a, MLIP-DFT relaxed atomic positions at a 5° twist showing Ti atoms in the top (light) and bottom (dark) interfacial layers, demonstrating the orthogonal screw dislocation network, with a magnified view on the right. b, Twist-angle dependence of the interface energy (blue) together with the computed and analytical dislocation lengths (orange). The background colour denotes the transition from well-defined dislocations to their absence. c–f, Dislocation lengths are measured using the interlayer distance as a signature. The analytical prediction given by d = (a/2)/sin(θ/2) (orange line) matches the measured dislocation lengths.

Sources indicate that a–d, HAADF-STEM image of the (110) cross-section of 7.5° (a,b) and 10° (c,d) twisted samples. Top and bottom images are independently sampled fields of view. The measured dislocation spacing d2 is 2.1 ± 0.2 nm in a,b and 1.5 ± 0.2 nm in c,d, agreeing well with the predictions for d2 = d/√2, as expected from this cross-section viewing plane (see text).

Phase-field model predicted polarization components Px, Py and Pz in blue, green and black, respectively, plotted as a function of the out-of-plane coordinate z in the 5° twisted bicrystal sampled at different positions (denoted by shapes). The middle panel highlights these points of interest overlaid on the dislocation network. The interface plane is located at z = 0 nm.

a, PDOS (left) and charge density isosurfaces at Ev − 0.3 eV (right) for a twist angle of 6.7°. b, Zoom-out of a but with isosurfaces at Ev − 0.06 eV highlighting dislocation node detail. The PDOS is further decomposed into node, dislocation line and bulk-like contributions.

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but promptly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

It has been revealed that they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

It has been revealed that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ states Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Industry observers note that like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Industry observers note that grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

According to recent reports, 'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady mentioned that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

It has been revealed that intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

City have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

Sources indicate that he utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

Sources indicate that the format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson claims, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

These are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

Recent findings suggest that unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

It has been revealed that some clubs have been known to give their content away for free, with Sky Sports taking two seasons of Mission to Burnley without paying. The driving force behind those moves is to promote brands. Under Alan Pace’s premiership, Burnley are staring at potential relegation to League One.

Vincent Kompany, then the Burnley manager, is understood to have been vexed at his portrayal as a hot-headed screamer. Brendan Rodgers cannot have been overly pleased with Being: Liverpool, which ended in public ridicule and comparisons to David Brent. Players at other clubs have confided that they hid from cameras.

‘You can’t be yourself, you never forget the cameras are there,’ says Grayson of his season alongside the makers of Sunderland 'Til I Die.

Salford's co-manager Anthony Johnson gives his players a dressing down in the BBC documentary.

According to recent reports, joey Barton, meanwhile, is still waiting for his moment – and may be for some time. Fleetwood Town commissioned their own team to chart his start in management and streaming giants Dazn purchased the rights.

Recent findings suggest that it was so close to being aired that Fleetwood held a premiere at Highbury Stadium for 100 supporters including the local mayor, only for one of Barton’s brushes with law enforcement in the intervening days to suspend the broadcast. Prolonged legal proceedings meant the idea was canned and Dazn’s licencing period expired.

Industry observers note that it was later resurrected, focusing in part on then Fleetwood owner Andy Pilley’s fraud trial – a crew followed him into court on day one – but was then shelved when a guilty verdict was handed down. Cameras are following clubs up and down the EFL from Birmingham to Cambridge via Sheffield Wednesday.

Grayson, for his part, refused to share his drive home from training with the crew and now admits that the ultimately unfavourable edit may have been a result of him not giving the production manufacturer what they wanted.

‘I did a presentation with the players with a flip chart and everybody thought it was an hour before kick-off of a league game,’ he says. ‘It was actually done at 11:30am before a pre-season game!

Industry observers note that 'That’s why I let them film it, because it was a pre-season game, and it had no real meaning. But they presented it in the doc as if it was before the first game of the season.

Recent findings suggest that 'Part of the severance when I was sacked was that I still needed to do some work for them. I did three different (choreographed) interviews in a London hotel with different shirts on after I’d been sacked, done as if they were filmed at the time.

‘People mentioned, “You didn’t come across that passionate about the club when you were talking about it”. Well, why would you when you were filming in November after you’d already been sacked? We were talking about deadline day in one of them. I’d already done something on that in August.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think they had sympathy with me, but also if they’d had more sympathy, they wouldn’t have even asked me to do it. I’ve spoken to managers since and they’ve gone, “F***ing hell, you did well to put up with that".'.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Fabian Delph leads a Manchester City inquest during an FA Cup defeat at Wigan - the only scene from the dressing room that made it into Amazon's documentary on the 2017-18 season.

Industry observers note that mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

It has been revealed that by his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

‘We won the league and we ended up getting sacked anyway,’ Johnson notes. ‘We went to meet Gary (Neville) and the board. We went upstairs in Hotel Football and a cameraman followed us. Obviously they knew what was going on. When we got to the room for the meeting, they wouldn't let the camera in.

‘I'm actually smiling thinking about it. The documentary followed me and Bern everywhere, eating food or whatever, and then when the day comes to sack us, they didn't want the camera in the room!

‘The conversation was fine in the room itself but I think the perception from the outside world looking in would've been: "What the f*** is that all about?”’.

It was known before the USMNT’s two-legged UEFA Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti that it would be Pochettino’s last two games, given that he has an agreement in place to take over the job at Manchester United vacated following Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

According to recent reports, the stars and stripes certainly gave him a fitting send-off, as they won the first leg 6-0 a few days ago and then completed the job with a 2-0 victory in Cincinnati last night. Pulisic got the first goal after a brace in the previous rout, and it was an incredible overhead kick.

According to recent reports, pulisic was actually overlooked by Pochettino for the September-October window – partly for fitness reasons – and he spoke to reporters after the game to share his thoughts after an emotional evening. He was called the ‘best player on the pitch’ by the US media, and his words are via MilanNews.

An overhead kick goal is pretty special….

“I’ve never scored a goal like that, it was special. Weston crossed the ball and it was the only thing I could really do, so I thought I had to give it a try. It was really nice to see the ball go in.”.

Is it nice to get a victory on Pochettino’s farewell day?

“Yes, obviously he’s leaving now, so it’s nice to end with a good performance and a nice win for the team.”.

How would you describe this particular group, a mix of veterans and young players?

Sources indicate that “It’s really nice. It’s been fun working with everyone. We got to meet some of the new guys, even some young talent, and obviously there’s still some of the same core group, so it’s a really great team. I really like where we are right now and I think we’re still growing and have a great future ahead of us.”.

“It was fantastic playing with him. He scored a goal, but also just for his overall play, making lots of runs and causing problems for the other team. He did a great job, fitting in with this team and making his mark.”.

What was Mauricio Pochettino’s farewell message to you this evening?

It has been revealed that “Simply that we have a truly extraordinary culture. We’ve built something truly special and that a bright future awaits us. And to continue that by letting the rest of the team support us.”.

Does it really matter who the coach is at this point?

A pretty good shift on his return; surprising he lasted until 90 minutes, when Magassa replaced him.

It has been revealed that should have taken a first-time shot with his right foot, but instead shifted onto his favoured left and scuffed the chance in the first half. Needs to produce more. Evidently Parker agrees as he was replaced by Castellanos on 57 minutes.

Struck the post with a right-footed effort as West Ham pressed for an equaliser. Had the beating of his full-back in the second half, making frequent runs down the right and crossing with his weaker foot. Several shots but lacked that killer punch – as did the whole attack.

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 12:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:11.

Arsenal reportedly remain interested in signing Brentford attacker Kevin Schade during the January transfer window.

Bolstering the left-wing position, along with bringing in a new striker, are priorities for Mikel Arteta, and several players have been linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium in recent weeks.

Schade joined the Bees in January 2023 and has since made 118 appearances for the club, scoring 25 goals.

The German attacker has made 10 Premier League appearances this season, starting nine of them, and has scored three goals so far.

According to TEAMTalk, Arsenal view Schade as a strong candidate to add depth and competition across their forward line.

Schade is primarily a left-sided forward but possesses the versatility to operate across the frontline, a quality that appeals to Arteta.

The winger is regarded as a realistic and proven Premier League option for the Gunners, given his ability to make an immediate impact.

While Arsenal's interest is genuine, any potential move would depend on Brentford's valuation and how Schade's contract negotiations with the club progress.

Schade has entered the final two years of his Brentford contract, and the club have reportedly opened talks with the player over a upcoming deal.

The Bees are said to be keen to offer him a newly introduced long-term contract on improved terms, underlining his growing importance in Keith Andrews's squad.

The Gunners could face competition from Premier League rivals Liverpool, who have reportedly emerged as serious contenders in the race for Schade.

Arsenal are also said to be keeping tabs on RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, although they would need to pay a substantial transfer fee to prise him away from the German club.

  • From Preston’s first corner, the fanbase was understandably apprehensive, knowing West Ham’s weaknesses from dead balls earlier in the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s familiar profligacy in front of goal came back to haunt them, as did their propensity to go behind in the first half of games as the points were shared at London Stadium this afternoon.

From Preston’s first corner, the fanbase was understandably apprehensive, knowing West Ham’s weaknesses from dead balls earlier in the season. Again the curse struck, with Piroe heading the ball over his own oncoming goal keeper’s fists, the ball then looping onto the post and allowing a gentle tap-in for Preston to take the lead.

Herrick rallied well after conceding early.

Recent findings suggest that the wheels could have come off for West Ham’s young goal keeper at that point: However, all credit to Herrick. It would have been very easy for his confidence to crumble after that early combi-cock-up, but he rallied well and even appeared to be smiling as the game went on, with several catches and a couple of really good saves surely meaning the shirt is his for the time being.

West Ham hit the post four times during a frenetic period in the first half when their intensity was high, but it seemed as though the ball simply would not go between the posts.

Recent findings suggest that familiar problems surfaced in the second half as the pace dropped and West Ham ran out of ideas, notably after Austbø had been substituted. Manor Solomon, looking very one-footed, simply ran inside and passed square. Frustratingly, the game slowed in pace in the last twenty minutes with the Hammers looking devoid of newly introduced ideas just at the time when they should have been upping the tempo.

It is clear that there’s still a shortage of pace in this side and with a build up that got slower as the game went on, West Ham’s bench looked as if it desperately needed an injection of Antonio-like pace to scare opponents and perhaps take on a shot!

A disappointment for the West Ham supporters, who booed their team off in the now time-honoured tradition as another two points went west. Against the bottom side.
